measurement.test: blocks the event loop for the whole synchronous DatabaseSync statement (with tolerance)
measurement.workload: 800000-row recursive CTE through sql-sqlite-node service.execSync (the accepted blocking facade)
measurement.runVariance: 236-246ms across two runs; the assertion is relative (timer must not have run during the statement, delay >= max(10ms, 50% of the statement)), not an absolute wall-time promise

red.conclusion: the guard fails if the path is no longer blocking

sqlSqliteNodeServiceDefaults.journal_mode: delete (SQLite default; service does not set it)
sqlSqliteNodeServiceDefaults.foreign_keys: 1 (node:sqlite DatabaseSync default; service does not set it)
sqlSqliteNodeServiceDefaults.setupPreserved: a per-store setup() setting WAL + synchronous NORMAL reads back wal/1

sqliteMemoryInitialization.busy_timeout: 0 on initializeSqliteMemory's own raw DatabaseSync connection (it does not call openSqliteDatabase)
sqliteMemoryInitialization.auto_vacuum: 2 / INCREMENTAL (explicit only for a new database, sqlite-memory/src/index.ts:2059)
sqliteMemoryInitialization.regularStoreOpen: openSqliteDatabase sets only busy_timeout=5000 (sqlite-memory/src/index.ts:179); journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys come from the file header and SQLite/node defaults
sqliteMemoryInitialization.restoreGap: VACUUM INTO backup: a backup is a delete-journal database; restore copies those bytes over the live store, so the restored journal_mode reads back delete, not the live store's WAL mode (pinned in the fence test)

drainFence.evidence: With an owner DatabaseSync handle open, restoreRuntimeState has no registry to consult: on Windows it fails only because the OS refuses the file replace (EPERM), not because of an owner fence; after closing the owner it succeeds. On POSIX the same call would be expected to replace the file while the owner is open. No test can prove a logical refusal because the code has none.
drainFence.wouldLive: a shared owner registry/lock at the sqlite-memory maintenance layer (around backupRuntimeState/deleteRuntimeState/restoreRuntimeState), because sql-sqlite-node's service owns per-connection handles and exposes no global owner registry; adding it is a product change and out of this slice.

noSubstitute.behavioral: an Effect transaction inserts a row and fails; the row count after the failed run is 0 (real SQL rollback)
noSubstitute.static: service.ts contains BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, no TxRef, no setTimeout; every Effect.runSync line only manages Ref open/owner state, never a pretend transaction

red.mutation: replaced BEGIN IMMEDIATE with SELECT 1 in the Effect transaction
red.observed: rollback test failed (SQLite service is closed / no real transaction)
red.conclusion: the test fails if the SQL transaction is replaced by non-transactional work

noSubstitute.memorySourcePinned: sqlite-memory/src/index.ts:167-179 pins SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 and PRAGMA busy_timeout; the retry waits are Atomics.wait, not a scheduled async substitute

redGreen.fenceNote: item 3 has no RED/GREEN pair because no logical owner fence exists; the characterization test in the same suite records the OS-only refusal and exact sites instead of inventing behaviour.
